title: Notebook, August: 16 mechanisms from 223 commits
excerpt: A month of git history reduced to its technical content: policy routing inside containers, idempotent namespace mutations, hysteresis and single-flight, closed-interval scans, positive-labelled validation sets, session identity binding. Symptom, mechanism, fix, verification, generalisation.

title: Grapple Dojo: putting a real human on 23 dots
excerpt: GrappleMap stores joint positions; a Mixamo rig wants bone rotations. I wrote the converter: a per-bone solver with no IK that stretches bones instead, and it ended up baking the walk cycles too.

title: The harness is all you need: an LLM that repairs 1,400 rules and decides nothing
excerpt: I put a language model inside a production maintenance pipeline. The model proposes, deterministic code verifies, a human approves. Tripling the model did nothing; narrowing what it sees doubled precision.

title: Shooting Range: resurrecting a 2016 Flash game with zero assets
excerpt: My first game was a .swf nothing can open anymore. I rebuilt it as one canvas and one script: every sprite drawn, every gunshot synthesized with Web Audio, and a five-line Render blueprint with no build step.

title: You probably don't need Redis: Postgres as your job queue
excerpt: The 2026 revival of "just use Postgres" is not hype. SKIP LOCKED for queues, LISTEN/NOTIFY for pub/sub, UNLOGGED tables for cache: the database you already run covers most of what you reach for Redis to do.

title: AI coding agents don't have a code problem, they have a context problem
excerpt: 2026's agents plan, code, test, and deploy on their own. The bottleneck moved from writing code to feeding them the right context and validating what comes back. Autonomy without a gate ships confident mistakes.

title: Before an agent touches production, give it a branch of the database
excerpt: Agents happily write and run schema migrations now. Point one at production directly and you have automated your worst outage. Give it an isolated branch, validate, then merge.

title: Fuzzy matching product names: Levenshtein, token scorers, and why you layer them
excerpt: You scraped a product page with no barcode. Match its URL slug to a million-row catalog by meaning, not spelling: edit distance as the floor, token scorers on top, candidates narrowed first.

title: Why Akamai is harder than Cloudflare
excerpt: People lump the big bot defenses together and waste weeks. Cloudflare is a gate you pass once; Akamai is a relationship you maintain, with a sensor payload it revalidates the whole time.

title: State machine, not saga
excerpt: When work spans processes, the first incident question is: where is this item right now? Track explicit states, and skip the saga you cannot afford until a real side effect demands it.

title: The proxy grid: your address is part of your identity
excerpt: You can get the TLS fingerprint perfect and still get blocked, because the address the request arrives on is a layer of the identity too, and defenses bind their trust to it.

title: The strangler fig: rebuild a live system without a rewrite
excerpt: The clean rewrite is the option everyone wants and the one that usually dies. Stand a new system around the old and retire it piece by piece, each step reversible.

title: Personas: give your scraper a coherent identity
excerpt: A Chrome User-Agent over a Firefox handshake is not a hybrid, it is an identity that cannot exist. Bind the layers into one object so the impossible one is unreachable.

title: The cookie handoff: let a browser solve it, then let curl fly
excerpt: An HTTP client cannot run JavaScript, yet a warmup beats defenses that demand it. The trick is splitting the work: a browser solves once, a fast client replays.

title: Find your own origin before someone else does
excerpt: A CDN only protects you if its shield cannot be walked around. Here is the audit an attacker would run against your origin, so you can run it first. Authorized targets only.

title: Why we split one pipeline into three services
excerpt: Fetch, parse, and store are three kinds of work with three resource profiles. One process forces them to share a fate they never shared in nature.

title: Declare your sort order and delete half your memory
excerpt: When producers declare sort order as a contract, consumers can pick a merge over a hash, and the state they must keep collapses from huge to constant.

title: Grapple Dojo: turning a grappling database into a turn-based game
excerpt: Grappling chess, built on GrappleMap: 843 real positions, 1,485 transitions, 3D stick figures, and a duel where you spot the real technique among decoys.

title: Why your scraper gets blocked: the six surfaces
excerpt: A correct User-Agent is not a disguise. Cloudflare and Akamai read six layers at once, and only about a fifth of them travel as bytes you control. Here is the whole stack.

title: Stack Panic: I turned the call stack into a furnace
excerpt: Real LeetCode problems fall into a furnace on an accelerating timer. Type the missing line or the spawns get permanently faster. Here is how the panic loop is built.

title: Config over code, and the ceiling only a machine can raise
excerpt: Moving behavior into configuration has a limit, and the limit is human. A language model in the maintenance loop moves that ceiling. It does not remove it.

title: GrappleMap: modeling grappling as a graph of positions
excerpt: A whole martial art as nodes and edges: positions are states, transitions are the moves between them. Notes from hacking on Eelis van der Weegen's GrappleMap.
